title: Quick Depression Test
summary: Ten personal questions about mood, interest, energy and everyday functioning.

landing.intro:
10 quick questions. Everyday patterns.
How many feel familiar?

about.body:
This ten-question self-check asks about low mood, loss of interest, energy, sleep, appetite, concentration, self-worth and daily functioning over the past two weeks. It groups your answers into a cautious pattern summary; it does not calculate whether you have depression.

Depression can affect people differently, and sleep problems, stress, grief, medication and physical health conditions may cause similar changes. A professional assessment considers severity, duration, daily impact, safety and possible alternative explanations.

steps: Choose the answer that best reflects the past two weeks.
Think about frequency and impact rather than one difficult day.
Reveal your personal mood summary after all ten questions.

about.disclaimer: For general information only. This is not a diagnostic test, validated depression screener or substitute for professional care. It cannot confirm or rule out depression or another condition. If symptoms persist or interfere with daily life, speak with a qualified healthcare professional. If you may harm yourself or cannot stay safe, contact local emergency services or a crisis service now.

stage-1.preAdCopy: Your ten answers have been reviewed and your cautious mood summary is ready to reveal.

profile-1.title: No Strong Pattern Appeared
profile-1.copy: Your answers did not highlight one dominant pattern of mood or functioning changes. That cannot rule out depression, and symptoms can vary over time. Seek professional advice if you remain concerned or something feels difficult to manage.

profile-2.title: Your Emotional Load May Need Attention
profile-2.copy: Your answers centred on sadness, emptiness, irritability, hopelessness or harsh self-judgement. If these changes persist, recur or feel difficult to manage, discussing them with a qualified healthcare professional is a sensible next step.

profile-3.tier: INTEREST OR ENERGY CHANGES STOOD OUT
profile-3.title: The Change May Be More Than Tiredness
profile-3.copy: Your answers highlighted reduced enjoyment, low energy, sleep, appetite or concentration changes. Many factors can contribute, but a persistent cluster is worth discussing with a qualified healthcare professional.

profile-4.title: Do Not Carry This Alone
profile-4.copy: Your answers suggest that mood or energy changes may be interfering with responsibilities, relationships or self-care. This result is not a diagnosis, but it is a strong reason to seek timely professional support. If you cannot stay safe, contact emergency or crisis support now.

depression-q1.question: Over the past two weeks, how often have you felt low, empty, irritable or hopeless?

answers.a3: On more than half the days
answers.a4: Nearly every day or with major impact

depression-q2.question: How much interest or enjoyment have you had in things you normally value?

answers.a4: Very little, and it affects daily life

depression-q3.question: How has your energy been recently?

answers.a4: So low that ordinary tasks are difficult

depression-q4.question: Has your sleep changed without a clear short-term reason?

answers.a3: Frequent insomnia, early waking or oversleeping
answers.a4: A major change that disrupts daily functioning

depression-q5.question: Has your appetite or eating pattern changed?

answers.a2: A small change on difficult days
answers.a3: A noticeable loss or increase in appetite
answers.a4: A major change affecting my health or routine

depression-q6.question: How easy is it to concentrate, remember details or make decisions?

answers.a2: Harder when my mood is low
answers.a3: Often difficult because of low energy
answers.a4: So difficult that work or daily tasks suffer

depression-q7.question: How often have guilt, worthlessness or harsh self-criticism taken over?

answers.a4: Nearly every day or with severe distress

depression-q8.question: Have you felt noticeably slowed down, restless or unable to settle?

answers.a3: Frequently alongside low mood or energy
answers.a4: Strongly enough to affect everyday activities

depression-q9.question: Have you withdrawn from people, responsibilities or activities?

answers.a3: Often because I lack energy or interest
answers.a4: Yes, and important parts of life are being affected

depression-q10.question: Which statement best describes the overall pattern?

answers.a2: Low mood has been the main change
answers.a3: Low energy or lost interest has been the main change
answers.a4: Several changes have persisted and interfere with daily life
